## Nvidia Frankfurt Shares Drop More Than 6% on Board Probe


Nvidia also faced a company-specific headline over the weekend. According to CNBC, Nvidia's board of directors opened an independent investigation into the spying allegations surrounding CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman that U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy, and a company spokesperson said Huang was committed to continuing as CEO without interruption. Nvidia's Frankfurt-traded shares were more than 6% lower in early European trading on Monday, and a proxy for the stock on Hyperliquid was down 2% over 24 hours, CNBC reported.


## Week Ahead: CPI Tuesday, Then CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials Earnings


Investors now face a busy calendar. CNBC said traders will watch the consumer price index on Tuesday and the producer price index on Friday for clues on the Fed's next move, while key AI-related[earnings reports](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) from CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials are also on deck. ## Strategists Watch AI Capex and Margins After the Nasdaq Selloff


Liz Ann Sonders, chief investment strategist at the Schwab Center for Financial Research, said the Nasdaq and[Nasdaq-100](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/nasdaq-100-how-the-index-works-and-who-gets-in/) are oversold after heavy de-risking by traders, CNBC reported. "Retail has not proven to be the dip buyers that they have been in the past," she said on CNBC's "Fast Money," adding that "we may not fully be washed out yet." She suggested the near-term focus should be on companies' capex plan adjustments and profit margin expectations.


Reuters also quoted strategists who still see AI as the market's central story. "We still think AI is the dominant theme in this bull market," said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services. Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist at LPL Financial, told Reuters that "AI has gone on trial several times in this cycle and come away with an innocent verdict," and added, "This week we saw a little bit of a knee-jerk reaction."
